headline: Finnish technology group Wärtsilä has won an order to build a 282-megawatt power plant on site at a data center project in the United States.
score_reason: Pool 5 kept: a company announcement with size, dates and a stated reason, but no named customer, site or price.
importance_line: Data center developers, and the utilities whose grids they would otherwise join, are affected, as the company says slow grid connections are pushing developers to build their own plants, but it is Wärtsilä's own announcement and the customer, site and price are not disclosed.
summary: Wärtsilä, a Finnish technology group that makes engines and power plants, says in a press release that it has won an order to supply a 282-megawatt (282 million watts) on-site power plant, built at the data center itself and running on 15 Wärtsilä 50SG engines, for a data center project being developed by an unnamed major US independent power producer (a company that generates power for sale), with delivery due in 2028 and full operation expected in 2029. The company, which calls this its seventh US data center order and puts its US data center power sales at more than 3 gigawatts, says grid limits and long connection waits are pushing developers to generate their own power.
notes: The source is the company's own press release (Wärtsilä is both the reporter and a party to the order); the customer is unnamed, so there is no independent confirmation. Water, fuel and efficiency claims in the release are the company's own and were left out.
